t: Tesla's Austin charging hub plans 80 wireless chargers, likely for the Cybercab
d: A permit for a large Tesla charging lot in south Austin includes 48 V4 Superchargers and, in a second phase, 80 wireless chargers. Here is why that points to the Cybercab.

t: Giga Shanghai builds its 6 millionth battery pack, just 279 days after the 5 millionth
d: Tesla's Shanghai factory has assembled six million battery packs. The last million took about nine months, as exports from the plant hit records while sales inside China fall. Here is what the milestone shows about Tesla's biggest factory.

t: SpaceX closes $60 billion Cursor deal: what the AI coding tool means for Grok, and for Tesla
d: SpaceX has completed its all-stock takeover of Cursor, the maker of a popular AI coding assistant. The team will now work on Grok, the assistant in Tesla's cars.

t: Tesla launches a Certified Pre-Owned program in the US: 115-point inspection and a one-year warranty
d: Used Teslas sold through the new program get a check of more than 115 points, a one-year or 10,000-mile warranty and a history report. It is available in the US and Puerto Rico, not yet in Canada or Europe.

t: Two Powerwalls for $35 a month: Tesla bundles a home battery lease with its Texas power plan
d: Tesla Electric now offers Texans a lease on two Powerwalls with no installation cost, at about $35 a month after a bill credit, if they sign up for its Backup electricity plan. Here is how the deal works and what the catches are.

t: 'All cars will have Starlink': Musk's prediction, and the Cybercab with a built-in dish
d: Elon Musk says every car will eventually connect via Starlink, and photos show a Cybercab with an antenna built into the rear. Here is what is known about satellite internet in Teslas.

t: First Megapack 3 rolls off the line at Tesla's new Texas Megafactory
d: Tesla has started production of the Megapack 3 in Brookshire, near Houston, in a factory designed for 50 GWh a year. Here is what is new about the battery and why it matters.

t: Tesla wins court order to recover Cybertruck tooling from supplier Angstrom, and Giga Texas output picks up
d: A federal judge has given Tesla the right to enter supplier Angstrom Automotive's closing plant in Troy, Texas, and take back the dies and casting tools it needs to build the Cybertruck. A flyover the next day suggested production is recovering.

t: Tesla Powerwall 3 goes on sale in Japan, with subsidy registration and installs from autumn
d: Tesla has started selling the Powerwall 3 home battery in Japan. The 13.5 kWh unit delivers 9.69 kW, is registered for government subsidies and should be installed from September or October.

t: No Grok in China: Tesla rolls out ByteDance's Doubao and DeepSeek to the Model 3, Model Y, Model S and Model X
d: A new software update brings a Chinese-built AI assistant to Tesla's main models in China. In the rest of the world, the same job is done by Grok from Musk's own AI company.

t: Tesla builds its 10 millionth car, a Model Y from Fremont, six years after its first million
d: A Diamond Black Model Y from the Fremont Factory in California is Tesla's 10 millionth vehicle. The first million took 12 years; the next nine million took just over six.

t: Tesla's first big European FSD safety report: 65 million km and six collisions
d: Tesla says FSD (Supervised) was 5.2 times safer than manual driving across five EU countries. Here are the numbers behind the claim, how they compare, and what they cannot tell us yet.

t: The Vegas Loop in numbers: $5-10 million a mile, 40,000 riders on peak days, and machines at a quarter of their target speed
d: A Boring Company executive has shared rare figures on cost, ridership and digging speed. What they show about the Tesla-powered tunnel network, and what they leave out.

t: FSD v14 Lite for Hardware 3: what older Teslas get, and what they never will
d: Tesla has started a wide rollout of FSD v14 Lite to cars with Hardware 3. It brings much of v14's smoother driving to older Model 3 and Model Y, but HW3 has reached its ceiling.

t: Tesla Q2 2026 results: revenue holds, but profit shrinks as spending soars
d: Tesla's second quarter showed $28.2 billion in revenue, earnings well below expectations, a 1.4% operating margin and negative free cash flow. Here are the key numbers and what drove them.

t: Frontier's owner picks Starlink for more than 1,000 planes: what the airline deal says about Starlink's next market
d: Indigo Partners, which owns Frontier, Wizz Air, Volaris, JetSMART and Cebu Pacific, will fit Starlink to more than 1,000 aircraft. The first Frontier planes are due in early 2027.

t: Tesla delivers 480,126 cars in Q2 2026, up 25% and far above Wall Street's estimate
d: Tesla's second-quarter deliveries jumped 25% from a year earlier to 480,126, ending a two-year run of falling sales and beating analyst expectations by about 74,000 cars. Energy storage reached 13.5 GWh.

t: Tesla settles Optimus trade secret lawsuit with robot hand startup Proception
d: Tesla has dropped its case against former Optimus engineer Jay Li and his startup Proception after a confidential settlement. The same day, Proception announced an $11 million seed round for its robot hands.

t: Tesla settles lawsuit over first known pedestrian death linked to FSD
d: Tesla has quietly settled the lawsuit over a 2023 Arizona crash in which a Model Y using Full Self-Driving killed a 71-year-old woman. The terms are secret, but the federal safety probe it started continues.

t: Tesla signs 25 GWh Megapack deal with NatPower for battery parks in the UK and Italy
d: Developer NatPower has agreed a multi-year deal with Tesla for more than 25 GWh of battery storage across five sites in Britain and Italy, worth an estimated $4-5 billion to build. It is one of the largest storage orders ever announced in Europe.

t: Tesla cuts Powerwall lease prices in Massachusetts and Connecticut, if owners let it run their batteries
d: Tesla now offers cheaper, no-money-down Powerwall leases in Massachusetts and Connecticut that come with automatic virtual power plant enrolment. In return, Tesla can dispatch the batteries 70 to 100 times a year.

t: Starship V3 flies for the first time: the ship hits its target, the booster crashes into the Gulf
d: SpaceX's first third-generation Starship launched from a new pad in Texas, deployed 22 dummy satellites and splashed down in the Indian Ocean. The Super Heavy booster failed to relight its engines.

t: End of an era: the last Tesla Model S and Model X roll off the line in Fremont
d: After 14 years of the Model S and 11 of the Model X, production has ended. The final car was a black Model S signed by the workers, and a 350-car Signature Edition says goodbye.

t: Cybertruck recalls: a new wheel recall, and what the 2025 recall wave means for owners
d: Tesla is recalling 173 Cybertrucks with 18-inch steel wheels over cracking stud holes. It follows three recalls covering nearly 116,000 trucks in 2025. Here is what owners should check.

t: Anthropic rents all of Colossus 1: why Grok's maker is leasing its first supercomputer to a rival
d: SpaceX's AI unit will hand the full capacity of its first Memphis data center, more than 300 MW and 220,000 Nvidia GPUs, to Claude developer Anthropic. Here is what the deal involves and how it connects to Tesla.

t: Tesla reports Musk's 2025 pay at $158 billion, yet he received nothing: the filing explained
d: Tesla's new filing values Elon Musk's 2025 pay at a record $158 billion, almost all of it accounting value for awards he has not earned. Here is what the number means, and what else the filing showed.

t: Tesla Robotaxi expands to Dallas and Houston, its first new cities after Austin, without a safety monitor
d: Tesla has started its Robotaxi service in Dallas and Houston, the first expansion beyond Austin and the Bay Area. The service areas are small and Tesla shared few details, but the cars run with nobody in the driver's seat.

t: Delaware court throws out three shareholder suits against Musk and Tesla's board: they belong in Texas
d: A Delaware judge has dismissed three derivative lawsuits over insider trading, AI and Twitter claims, enforcing the Texas forum rule Tesla adopted when it left Delaware.

t: Netherlands becomes the first European country to approve Tesla FSD Supervised
d: Dutch regulator RDW has approved Tesla's Full Self-Driving (Supervised) after more than 18 months of testing. It is valid in the Netherlands only for now, and the driver stays fully responsible.

t: Last call for the Model S and Model X: custom orders closed, inventory nearly gone
d: Tesla has stopped taking custom orders for its two flagship cars. The Model X appears sold out in the US and the Model S Plaid is hard to find. Here is what is still possible.

t: UK car tax from April 2026: the £50,000 'luxury car' limit for EVs, and which Teslas now escape it
d: From April 1, 2026, electric cars only pay the UK's expensive car supplement above a £50,000 list price. Here are the new rates, which Model 3 and Model Y versions benefit, and what to check on your own car.

t: All 11 xAI co-founders have now left: what Musk's 'rebuild' of Grok's maker means for Tesla
d: With Ross Nordeen and Manuel Kroiss gone, none of the researchers who founded xAI with Elon Musk in 2023 remain. Tesla has $2 billion and its in-car assistant riding on the outcome.

t: NHTSA escalates Tesla FSD sun glare and fog probe to 3.2 million vehicles
d: US safety regulator NHTSA has upgraded its investigation into how Full Self-Driving handles poor visibility to an engineering analysis, the last step before a possible recall. Here is what it found so far.

t: Starlink passes 10,000 satellites in orbit at the same time: what the milestone means, and the Tesla link
d: A Falcon 9 launch from California on March 16 pushed SpaceX's Starlink constellation past 10,000 working satellites in orbit at once, less than seven years after the first batch.

t: Tesla can now sell electricity to British homes: Ofgem grants a supply licence
d: Ofgem has given Tesla a licence to supply electricity to households and businesses in England, Scotland and Wales. There is no launch date or tariff yet, but the model is likely to follow Tesla Electric in Texas.

t: Vegas Loop carries 82,000 riders in Teslas during CONEXPO, as Prufrock-2 finishes a record 2.28-mile tunnel
d: The Boring Company's Las Vegas tunnels moved about 82,000 passengers during the five-day CONEXPO-CON/AGG trade show, and its Prufrock-2 machine completed the longest single Vegas Loop tunnel so far.

t: Tesla's VP of Finance Sendil Palani leaves after 17 years, the latest in a long line of senior exits
d: Sendil Palani, who joined Tesla when the company was close to collapse in 2008, has announced he is leaving. His exit follows a string of departures of long-serving executives over the past year.

t: Tesla cuts Cybertruck prices: new AWD base model from $59,990, Cyberbeast under $100,000
d: Tesla's updated 2026 Cybertruck lineup brings a cheaper dual-motor version and cuts about $15,000 from the top trims. Here is what you get, and what was removed.

t: Nevada lawmakers question Vegas Loop safety: 17 OSHA complaints, dropped fines and wastewater penalties
d: A legislative hearing put The Boring Company's Las Vegas tunnels under scrutiny over worker injuries and environmental violations. The facts, both sides, and why it matters for the Tesla-powered Loop.

t: Cybertruck arrives in the Middle East: about 60 trucks delivered in Dubai on day one
d: Tesla has started Cybertruck deliveries in the UAE, its first market in the Middle East, and opened orders in Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Jordan and Israel. Here are the prices and why Europe is still off-limits.

t: Cybertruck sales almost halved in 2025: the numbers and the reasons
d: According to Cox Automotive, US Cybertruck sales fell 48% to about 20,200 in 2025. Here is what went wrong, from the end of the tax credit to price and politics.

t: Tesla's former Optimus chief Milan Kovac joins Hyundai's Boston Dynamics, days after the new Atlas debut
d: Milan Kovac, who led Tesla's Optimus humanoid robot programme until June 2025, has been appointed adviser and outside director at Boston Dynamics. The move strengthens one of Optimus's most direct rivals just after Atlas was shown at CES 2026.

t: Tesla's Robovan could carry crowds in the Vegas Loop, but only once the tunnels reach 1,200 Teslas
d: The Boring Company's president says the 20-seat Robovan would handle event surges at Allegiant Stadium and the Sphere after the network is fully built. What is planned, and what is still uncertain.

t: Starlink will lower 4,400 satellites from 550 to 480 km in 2026: why SpaceX is moving half its fleet
d: SpaceX says a lower orbit means dead satellites fall back within months instead of years. The reasons behind the move, the December debris incident, and the link to Tesla.
